# Data and lineage

```{r}
#| include: false
source(here::here("chapters", "_setup.R"))
raw_md5 <- unname(tools::md5sum(here::here("data", "raw", "licorice_gargle.csv")))
n_missing <- sum(is.na(clean$pain_30min))
bounds <- results$bounds
worst <- bounds[bounds$scenario == "Worst case for licorice", ]
robust <- all(bounds$upper < 1)
```

## Source

The raw file `data/raw/licorice_gargle.csv` was exported once from the
`medicaldata` R package (see `scripts/01_get_raw_data.R`) and is never edited.
Its MD5 checksum is `r raw_md5`; `scripts/02_make_analysis_data.R` refuses to
run if the bytes change (D-005).

## Lineage

Each step is a function in `R/` with tests in `tests/testthat/`.

```{r}
#| echo: false
knitr::kable(lineage, col.names = c("Step", "Rows", "File"))
```

- **raw → clean** (`clean_licorice()`): recode numeric codes to labeled
  factors using the codebook, rename pain variables, and validate ranges.
  An unexpected code stops the pipeline instead of silently becoming `NA`.
- **clean → long** (`to_long()`): one row per patient per assessment, with
  `any_pain` defined as a pain score above zero. Missing scores are dropped.

## Missing data

The public dataset has `r nrow(clean)` patients; the study enrolled one more
(see the open questions in Chapter 1). Of those in the file, `r n_missing`
have no post-operative outcomes at any time point, one in each arm. They are
excluded from outcome analyses (complete case; D-006) and remain in the
baseline description.

Could they change the primary result? Setting both missing outcomes to the
values least and most favourable to licorice gives:

```{r}
#| label: tbl-missing-bounds
#| tbl-cap: "Primary odds ratio: complete case and extreme assumptions about missing outcomes."
knitr::kable(
  data.frame(
    Scenario = bounds$scenario,
    `Odds ratio (95% CI)` = fmt_or_cell(bounds$or, bounds$lower, bounds$upper),
    `p-value` = fmt_p(bounds$p_value),
    check.names = FALSE
  )
)
```

The worst case for licorice gives `r fmt_or(worst)`, so the missing
outcomes `r if (robust) "cannot change" else "could change"` the conclusion.

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| results: asis
fit_warnings_note(results, "Missing-outcome bounds")
```
